facts.content: Patient complains of 'aching all over' and fatigue for 6 weeks.
facts.source_text: CC: “aching all over”, fatigue x 6 wks

facts.content: Symptoms began about 2 weeks after returning from a holiday in the US.
facts.source_text: Onset ~2 wks after return from US holiday (end Jan/early Feb)

facts.content: Patient experiencing generalized myalgias including shoulders, back, hips, and knees.
Patient reports decreased energy and appetite, with no weight change.
Patient has occasional mild headache.
Patient had a rash on the left calf mid-February, faint, minimal itch, resolved in about 2 weeks, preceded by sore throat possibly with low-grade fever.
facts.source_text: Rash post L calf mid-Feb; faint, minimal itch, resolved in ~2 wks; preceded by sore throat ± low-grade fever

facts.content: Patient denies cough, shortness of breath, chest pain, ear, nose, and throat symptoms, gastrointestinal or genitourinary changes, neurological deficits, joint swelling.
facts.source_text: Denies cough, SOB, chest pain, ENT sx, GI or GU changes, neuro deficits, joint swelling

facts.content: Patient has a history of asthma and hay fever.
Patient uses an inhaled preventer twice daily.
Patient takes over-the-counter antihistamine.
Patient works in health tech, lives with wife, is a non-smoker, drinks alcohol occasionally, and is an active walker.
facts.source_text: works in health tech; lives with wife; non-smoker; occasional etOH; active walker

facts.content: Patient has reduced recent exercise.
Fatigue and myalgias for 6 weeks might be due to Lyme disease, post-viral condition, or other systemic etiology.
facts.source_text: Fatigue & myalgias x 6 wks – ?Lyme disease vs post-viral vs other systemic etiology

facts.content: Resolved calf rash is likely erythema migrans from a tick bite.
facts.source_text: Resolved calf rash – likely erythema migrans (tick bite)

facts.content: Asthma is stable on preventer.
Allergic rhinitis is controlled on antihistamine.
Arrange blood tests including FBC, U&E, LFT, Lyme serology, TFTs, and others per local fatigue panel.
facts.source_text: Arrange bloods: FBC, U&E, LFT, Lyme serology, TFTs, others per local fatigue panel

facts.content: If Lyme disease tests positive, start appropriate antibiotics such as doxycycline.
facts.source_text: If Lyme + → start appropriate abx (e.g., doxycycline)

facts.content: Continue inhaler twice daily and reinforce adherence.
Use antihistamine as needed for hay fever.
Patient advised to return sooner if symptoms worsen or if new neurological, fever, or joint symptoms develop.
facts.source_text: Return sooner if worsening, new neuro sx, fever, joint swelling

facts.content: Follow-up by phone in 1 week post-results.
